quest.title: Memories That Should Not Exist
quest.description: You have heretofore been unable to track down the missing man, but you encounter a familiar figure after the creatures of the Abyss Order emerge...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1000, Mora x44000, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a second... That person, it's... Dainsleif!

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Ah, it's you two...

dialogues.speaker: Atossa
dialogues.text: Oh, a friend of yours?

dialogues.speaker: Atossa
dialogues.text: Well, I'll leave you all to it, then. I should head back to the village to check up on Chief Amadhiah and the others, anyway. See you later!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep! See you later, Atossa!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why do you always have to pop up out of nowhere like that!? Is it your life's mission in life to jumpscare us or something?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: It's hardly personal... or intentional, for that matter. As long as you and I are both in pursuit of the Abyss Order, we're bound to cross paths.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, so you're here to investigate the Abyss Order, then! That would explain the monsters you were fighting just now...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Naturally. Hold on... Are you not here for the same purpose?

choices.text: We're also on their tail...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Hm, no matter. It may have taken you a while to catch on, but I'm sure you've also realized by now... That there's something strange about this place.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: The Abyss Order is most certainly planning something in this area... or worse, their plan could already be in motion.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you think the Abyss Order is behind the Hilichurl activity in the area?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: As things stand, I highly doubt that is their primary motive. I would imagine the increased Hilichurl activity is merely a byproduct of whatever it is they're really trying to accomplish.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, the Hilichurl activity is causing a lot of problems for the people here. We should stick around for a while and protect the village, don't you think?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: The best way to protect them is by figuring out what the Abyss Order is truly planning. That is how we prevent further tragedy.

choices.text: Well, let's see what more we can learn from the villagers.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: And you shall have them. I never intended to hide anything from you.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Don't worry... There should be ample time to talk.

choices.text: And after that... You also owe us many answers.
But, I'll admit, we ran into them on accident.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You return to Vimara Village to gather intel based on what you've learned. You question the villagers until, eventually, the sky grows dark...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Ah, so that was the commission that brought you here to Vimara Village...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: "Someone who seems to only exist in people's memories"... That is indeed quite intriguing. I would agree that it's unlikely you have a simple missing person's case on your hands. However, any possible connection to the Abyss Order is still unclear.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: It appears all we have by way of clues is increased Hilichurl activity, and that is certainly not much to go off of.

choices.text: Well, then...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Right! That mysterious voice {F#she}{M#he} heard in {F#her brother's}{M#his sister's} memory... The one who called himself a Sinner... Who is he?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, let me ask you this... Do you believe your sibling to have betrayed you?

choices.text: #I want to have faith in {M#her}{F#him}.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Hmm... I sense hesitation in your words. After all, you still haven't figured out the whole truth of what happened.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: There's still hope for the two of you to reconcile. Irreparable damage has not yet been done.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: The Sinner you wish to know about... His situation is different. He and his fellow sinners have long betrayed me, and long betrayed their nation.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: His name is Vedrfolnir, "The Visionary."

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: I'm loath to admit it, but... He is also my kin. My older brother.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Your... brother?

choices.text: What happened between the two of you?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: There were five of them... The Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: "The Wise" Hroptatyr, "The Visionary" Vedrfolnir, "Gold" Rhinedottir, "The Foul" Surtalogi, and "Rächer of Solnari" Rerir.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: No matter how eroded my memory may become, I will never forget their names... One day... I shall have my vengeance.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait! Some of those names sound really familiar... Rhinedottir is the one who created Albedo, Surtalogi is Skirk's master...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And the one we just learned about... Dain's brother, Vedrfolnir... If he was the voice of the Sinner, then the one who inspired Chlothar to create the Abyss Order... was him!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Somehow, everything is connected...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (If that's true, then the stone slates we found in that ruin in Fontaine... The ones that outlined Fontaine's prophecy... That was likely Vedrfolnir's doing as well.)

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: They were once people of great esteem in Khaenri'ah, those who carried the hopes of the nation. They were the best of their peers, outstanding in their respective fields...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: The six of us, together... We should have been the ones to prevent the disaster, the ones to stop the Vinster King from continuing to rock the foundation of the world.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Yet, deep within, the five of them craved something more. They could not resist the call of the Abyss, and divided among themselves a power that could destroy the world.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: So they became Sinners, but also transcendent beings, each in possession of world-shattering power.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: And when the cataclysm occurred, not one of them stood up in defense of their nation, not one came forward to prevent the tragedy... And for that, they shall never have my forgiveness.

choices.text: And then...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: ...Indeed. If they are not stopped, the day is sure to come when they will also betray the entire world.

choices.text: It must be hard to talk about all of this.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Of course. As I said, I never intended to hide anything from you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, Dain, what have you been looking into all this time?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: I've continued to investigate the questions surrounding the Loom of Fate. It's been quite some time since the initial operation was launched.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: By retrieving the eye of the first Field Tiller, we were able to stop part of their plan from coming to fruition...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, Paimon remembers! Weren't they gonna use it to corrupt Osial and make a god or something...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Indeed... However, it's obvious that was just some kind of technical experiment...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: The eye was integral to their plan, yet somehow, despite failing to obtain it, they've skipped the experimental phase and found some other way to keep moving forward.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: There are many signs pointing to that effect...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then, what should we do? It's not too late, is it?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Our most pressing concern... is to determine the purpose of the Loom of Fate. From there, we'll be able to deduce the Abyss Order's true objective.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Based on the intel I've gathered so far, I suspect the Loom of Fate is related to the Ley Lines in some way.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Ley Lines?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, you were able to observe your sibling's memories last time, yes? I believe that was due to the fact that the Ley Lines in that area were unstable.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: My recent investigation has shown that Abyss Order activity in a particular area is usually followed by a series of issues with the Ley Lines.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And one of the things that flows through the Ley Lines... are memories.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, then our commission here in Vimara Village... The person who seems to exist only in people's memories... Could it be connected?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Memories... Ley Lines... The Loom of Fate... The missing person that doesn't seem to exist...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (What's the connection between all this?)

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: It's certainly possible. I'll join your investigation tomorrow. This missing person's case could very well turn out to be the key to unraveling these mysteries.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, if we're teaming up with Dain again, we're gonna need all the energy we can get! Let's try investigating somewhere a little further away tomorrow.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *yawn*... So tired... Paimon used way too much brain juice yesterday. It's all Dain's fault, saying all that complicated stuff...

choices.text: I didn't sleep well, either...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, let's go find Dain. We've got a lot to do today.

choices.text: My head's a mess.
But thank you for telling me.
My sibling came into contact with your brother.
What really happened in Khaenri'ah back then?
In a manner of speaking, yeah.
How about the intel you promised me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, Dain? Hellooo... Dain! Why are you just zoning out over here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did something happen?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's wrong, Dain?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: The missing person from your commission... Could you describe them to me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, uh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Young guy, early twenties... Seriously, Dain... What's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: There appear to be certain memories in my mind that weren't there before...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Memories... of him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Maybe... Maybe we just talked too much about him yesterday, and you had a weird dream or something?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: No. It wasn't a dream. They're memories... memories that suddenly appeared in my mind after I woke up...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: And I'm certain I've never met this person before.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, what exactly did you "remember"?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: I remember...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: ...Handing him the eye of the first Field Tiller.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whaaaat!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Okay, so this missing person definitely has something to do with the Abyss Order, then...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Indeed. And it appears he possesses the ability to "implant" memories into the minds of others.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How is that even possible...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, then... All the memories the villagers have of him... Could they be fake too? Maybe they never knew him at all...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But why would he do something like that...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Whatever the Abyss Order is planning, an important truth has been revealed to us this morning...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What sort of truth?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: That their goal... is still to obtain the eye of the first Field Tiller. They haven't stopped searching for it.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: I am the only person who knows its location. Perhaps implanting that particular memory was an attempt to interfere with my mind in some way...

choices.text: Is the eye still safe?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Your concerns are not entirely unfounded. I don't believe the Abyss Order is capable of altering reality like that just yet...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: However, considering their single-minded pursuit of the eye, I would say an equal level of caution is in order on our part.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Come with me. We must check whether the eye is still in our possession.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, so you're going to take us to where you hid it?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (...But, what if someone follows us? If we go straight there, and someone is on our tail, aren't we just exposing the eye's location?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Maybe that's the reason the Abyss Order implanted that memory in the first place... To force Dain to confirm the eye's location...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Given what I know of him, though, I'm sure Dain has already thought of that possibility... It seems like he might already have a plan...)

choices.text: Let's go.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: ...Of course.

choices.text: Lead the way, Dain.
What if that "memory" is real?

talks.objective: Go to the place where the "Field Tiller's Eye" is hidden

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you hid it way out here! Not an easy place to discover, that's for sure.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, let's go check to see if it's safe!

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, wait...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hm?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: ...We've no time to lose. Let's head inside.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (What was Dain going to tell me just now...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, wait up!

talks.objective: Enter the place where the "Field Tiller's Eye" is hidden
Enter the depths of the ruin

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like we can't go any further...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Be on your guard. I sense the presence of the Abyss!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's the Abyss Order! They're here!

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Just as I suspected... The false memories were a trap. The Abyss Order just wanted to follow us here...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Now that they're in the vicinity, we should have a chance to see...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Argh...!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dain? What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Can you feel that? There's been a disturbance in the Ley Lines. It must be the work of the Abyss...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, you must be really sensitive to that sort of thing. Paimon doesn't feel it...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: You two, do as I say... Use that mechanism over there and leave this place.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Leave you here on your own? Will you be alright?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: The Abyss Order is putting something in motion. If you return to Vimara Village, I suspect you might finally have the opportunity to locate the missing villager.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: ...Just think of it as a way to divide and conquer.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Alright.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Dain does have a point...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (But, something still feels off... What am I missing...?)

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Hmph... I knew going along with your trap would be the only way to meet with you face to face.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: You risked your safety and that of the eye...

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: That's quite the gamble, Dainsleif... But I believe that I am the one walking into a trap laid by the Twilight Sword.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: So you came here all on your own? What about those followers of yours?

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: When the Twilight Sword is prepared for battle, any army I could send would only be marching to their doom... Better that I face you alone.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: I know you must have a lot to say...

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: ...But, if it's a conversation you want, you'll have to defeat me first.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You return to Vimara Village to gather intel based on what you've learned. You question the villagers until, eventually, the sky grows dark...
